acceptance_criteria: AC-1 Isolation of the choice-list probe on the canonical copy. The probe spawns the interpreter with -I -S. Measured, not asserted: under the port's flags no site-packages entry is left on sys.path, and under -I alone there is one, on every interpreter the host carries.

AC-2 Isolation of the choice-list probe on the packaged copy. The same two flags, in the same probe, verified THROUGH THE LIVE PUBLIC PYTHON SHIM 04-validate-handoff/eval-a-skill/scaffold-eval.py, not through a direct import of the packaged .mjs.

AC-3 Compiled-vs-packaged parity. For the same interpreter and the same question, the canonical copy and the packaged copy render BYTE-IDENTICAL choice lists, and the packaged copy's output is byte-identical to the canonical copy's. Asserted, not assumed.

AC-4 Unchanged public behaviour. The port's rendered error line, its exit code and its stdout are byte-identical before and after, for every input the existing parity corpus exercises. The change alters only WHICH interpreter output the port is willing to believe, never what the port emits.

AC-5 The read rule and the rendering are observable, and the suite pins the specific properties enumerated. This is NOT a claim of complete mutation coverage, and the goal does not assert one. Killed: dropping -S (A), reverting the read to the old stderr.includes form (C), dropping the invalid-choice marker from the shape check (G), rendering an empty choice list (D), always rendering the quoted form (E), always rendering the bare form (F). Survivor: dropping -I while keeping -S (B) — with -S alone the site module never runs and site.py is what imports sitecustomize, so -S alone already prevents every sitecustomize vector; the suite pins the property that matters and cannot distinguish -I -S from -S alone. The suite therefore does NOT pin that the PYTHON* environment and PYTHONHOME cannot change the stdlib the probe measures; that is AC-13.

AC-6 The no-interpreter control is meaningful. The control runs on a PATH that holds node and nothing else, ASSERTS that no python3 is resolvable on that PATH, and only then asserts the conservative quoted rendering. A control that cannot find an interpreter is not evidence that a missing interpreter is handled.
AC-7 The controls are live. The startup noise really lands on stderr after the interpreter's own message when nothing isolates it, and a pristine interpreter is not polluted.
AC-8 The suite cannot pass vacuously. An empty interpreter inventory is a failure, not a skip.

AC-9 The packaged source map's disposition is recorded: 04-validate-handoff/eval-a-skill/lib/scaffold-eval.mjs.map is left byte-unchanged, and the record states that it is a historical artifact of an earlier compilation, that its mappings are not authoritative, and that the packaged copy is maintained by manual dual-path translation of the canonical source.

AC-10 TDD evidence, same command, both legs, with the red leg exercising the newly delivered path. One command, bash tests/e6_scaffold_eval_probe_test.sh, recorded red then green at .ai/evidence/probe-isolation.json by tdd-evidence.sh. The red leg is that same command run against the PRE-GOAL-CHANGE PRODUCT BYTES with this goal's test file present. The test file must contain an assertion that exercises the PACKAGED PUBLIC ENTRYPOINT through 04-validate-handoff/eval-a-skill/scaffold-eval.py, and the red leg must fail ON THAT ASSERTION — the packaged copy's defect is independent of the canonical copy's, so a red leg that only exercises the canonical copy proves nothing about the delivered path. The red output must show the packaged assertion failing SEPARATELY from the canonical assertions. The red leg additionally covers the -S mechanism on the canonical copy: against the pre-goal-change bytes the site-packages sitecustomize case fails, because -I alone does not remove the interpreter's own site-packages from sys.path. The earlier native canonical-only RED/GREEN is preserved as EARLIER evidence and cannot supply this newly required RED; no RED/GREEN run is authorised by this criterion, and preserved WIP must not be overwritten to reconstruct it.

AC-11 Green at head. bash tests/run-tests.sh, prek run --all-files and git diff --check pass at the implementation head, with the mutating parity harness run in a DISPOSABLE WORKTREE so that no tracked fixture is left dirtied, and with the interpreter environment isolated so that no measurement depends on a shared symlink.
AC-12 No drift. ts-build-drift is green and the compiled artifacts are exactly what tsc emits.

AC-13 The PYTHON* environment cannot change what the probe measures, and this criterion is satisfied only by a QUALIFIED PORT-BOUND ORACLE. The standalone interpreter mechanism control - comparing sys.flags.ignore_environment with and without isolation in a separately invoked interpreter - MAY remain as a correctly labelled PYTHON MECHANISM CONTROL, but it is NOT evidence for this criterion and must not be substituted for it: a standalone interpreter command explicitly supplied -I can report ignore_environment correctly EVEN WHEN THE PRODUCT'S OWN PROBE LOSES -I, so that control does not bind the port's invocation and does not establish that mutant B is killed. THIS CRITERION IS SATISFIED BY EITHER OF THE TWO QUALIFIED PROSPECTIVE ORACLE FORMS, AND BY NO OTHER: (FORM 1) ACTUAL-SPAWN OBSERVATION - unambiguously observe the argv/effective interpreter flags of the ACTUAL canonical and packaged choice-list probes, requiring -I AND -S, not merely equal flags or a standalone interpreter command, and distinguishing the choice-list probes from the separate version probes; OR (FORM 2) QUALIFIED STRUCTURAL GUARD ON BOTH LIVE SHIPPING SITES - unambiguously identify the executable choice-list spawn in scripts/lib/leaf/scaffold-eval.mjs and in 04-validate-handoff/eval-a-skill/lib/scaffold-eval.mjs, the latter being the artifact reached by the public Python shim, and assert that EACH actual site includes -I AND -S and that their required read rules are equivalent. CHECKING ONLY COMMENTS, AN UNRELATED VERSION PROBE, ONLY TYPESCRIPT SOURCE, OR EQUALITY WITHOUT ABSOLUTE FLAGS IS INSUFFICIENT. A behavioural companion - with PYTHONHOME pointing at a directory holding a different stdlib, the port still measures the default stdlib - is admitted IF AND ONLY IF it exercises the port's own probe. THIS CRITERION IS THE ONE THAT WOULD KILL MUTANT B (drop -I, keep -S). UNTIL IT IS WRITTEN AND OBSERVED, MUTANT B SURVIVES, AND NO DOCUMENT MAY SAY OTHERWISE; A FUTURE SUCCESSFUL GUARD DOES NOT REWRITE THE REPORTED SURVIVAL OR RETROACTIVELY QUALIFY IT AS GATE EVIDENCE. The standalone comparison may be retained ONLY as a labelled mechanism control, and NO MUTANT COVERAGE IS CLAIMED WITHOUT AN OBSERVED MUTANT RESULT.

AC-14 Absolute two-site isolation invariant at the two LIVE SHIPPING choice-list sites. Equality between the two copies' flags and read rules is NOT this criterion: both copies can agree while omitting -I, so an equality-only assertion does not establish isolation. AC-15 Interpreter authenticity. EVERY interpreter the suite measures is asserted to be a GENUINE CPYTHON BINARY: the resolved file's first bytes must be a Mach-O image (cf fa ed fe, or fe ed fa cf, OR THE UNIVERSAL ca fe ba be), an ELF image (7f 45 4c 46), or a Windows PE image (4d 5a), and NEVER a #! script; and the interpreter must report sys.implementation.name == "cpython". THE UNIVERSAL MAGIC IS REQUIRED, because the Apple system interpreter is a Mach-O universal binary. A SUBSTITUTED INTERPRETER THEREFORE FAILS THE SUITE BY NAME instead of agreeing with the port on a forged rendering. WITHOUT THIS CRITERION THE SUITE'S COMPARISON IS SELF-CONSISTENT BUT NOT AUTHENTICITY-CHECKING - the port's rendering is compared with the interpreter's rendering, so a stub that mimics argparse AGREES with the port and the comparison passes - which is the same class the D13 checker names capture_authenticity: "unverified". DISCLOSED LIMIT: these checks assert the SHAPE AND IDENTITY OF THE EXECUTED FILE, NOT ITS PROVENANCE - a substituted NATIVE EXECUTABLE CAN PASS THE IMAGE MAGIC AND REPORT sys.implementation.name == "cpython", AND NO INDEPENDENTLY TRUSTED EXPECTED DIGEST OR BINARY PROVENANCE IS SPECIFIED BY THIS CRITERION. The interpreter's actual provenance, its import resolution and its writable-resource boundary therefore remain subject to the executing stage's qualified runtime and guard contract, and are not established by these criteria.

AC-16 Interpreter stability. The suite records each interpreter's RESOLVED REALPATH before it is executed and RE-RESOLVES it after the run; a CHANGED REALPATH, OR A CHANGED FILE DIGEST, IS A FAILURE, NOT A SKIP. The measurement is valid only within the recorded observation window, and a mutation observed inside that window INVALIDATES the measurement, in which case the run is repeated. This is the custody criterion that a resolved path alone cannot supply, because a symlink into another lane's disposable tree can VANISH or CHANGE MID-RUN.
